chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who has a pledge (collateral) with him but does not know whose it is among the people. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that he sells it until its owner comes.' I said: 'He does not know whose it it is among the people.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there excess or deficiency in it?' I said: 'If there is excess or deficiency in it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is deficiency in it, it is easier for him; he sells it and is rewarded for what is deducted from his own wealth. And if there is excess in it, it is more difficult for him; he sells it and retains the excess until its owner comes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling a lost pledge when the owner is unknown?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides nuanced guidance on the stewardship of pledged goods, prioritizing the preservation of the owner's wealth by distinguishing between loss and gain. This ruling reflects the Shia legal principle of *adl* (justice) in commercial transactions, where the holder bears the risk of deficiency but must safeguard any surplus until the rightful owner is identified. It underscores the ethical obligation of trust (*amanah*) in Islamic finance, ensuring that temporary custodians do not profit at the expense of the owner's rights.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about the man who happened to have the security deposit with him, so he did not know for whom it was, from the people’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not like it that he sells it until its owner comes over’. I said, ‘He does not know for whom it is, from the people’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Therein is excess or deficiency?’ I said, ‘Supposing if there was an excess or a deficiency in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there was a deficiency in it, so it is easier. He can sell it, and he compensate the deficiency from his own wealth. However, if there was an excess in it, so it is more difficult upon him. He can sell it, and he would have to keep its excess until its owner comes over’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who had al-Rahn (security deposit) with him and did not know to whom it belonged. He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not like his selling it until the owner comes.’ I said, ‘He does not know who the owner is.’ He (the Imam) then asked, ‘Is there any increase or decrease in it?’ I then asked, ‘What happens if there is increase or decrease in it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If there is decrease, it is easier. He can sell it and complete the reduction from his own property. If there is increase in it, it is more difficult because he sells it and must keep the increase until its owner comes.’”
